role.altitude: The PV installer keeps inspecting roofs, choosing locations, equipment and protection devices, planning the work and checking every drawing and order; measuring every roof from scratch, drawing layouts by hand, counting parts and working out device ratings from tables shrink.
skills_to_grow: Checking design tool output against the roof and the standard
role.ambitious_version: An installer who arrives at the roof with a checked layout, parts list and single-line diagram, and spends the visit confirming instead of measuring.

tasks.short: Measure roof dimensions, pitch and orientation, assess shading, inspect the roof structure, and identify installation locations with proper orientation, area, solar access and structural integrity for PV arrays.

steps.what: PV installer measures roof dimensions, pitch and orientation
PV installer assesses shading and solar access over the year
PV installer inspects the roof structure and condition
PV installer identifies installation locations with proper orientation, area, solar access and structural integrity

tasks.design: Before the visit, the design tool takes roof outline, pitch and orientation from aerial imagery and height data, so on the roof the installer checks key dimensions instead of measuring everything. The tool computes shading over the year from surrounding objects, and the installer confirms it on site. Inspecting the structure and choosing the locations stay with the installer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every roof was measured and shading judged on site.
tasks.enabler_now: Design tools fed by aerial imagery and height data with sun-path shading.
tasks.still_hard: Roofs hidden by trees or recently changed.
tasks.human_edge: Feeling that a roof deck is too soft to carry panels.
tasks.altitude: Less measuring; judging the roof stays.

reach.learn: Whether quotes from aerial data hold up on site.

evidence.claim: Design tools can take roof geometry from aerial imagery and compute shading from height data.

assumptions: Boundary: choosing where arrays go; mounting methods (task 17755) and system design (task 17749) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1 and s2: recent aerial imagery and height data for about 80% of addresses; older or changed roofs are measured in full; s1 and s2 are priced at that share.
Inspecting and choosing keep their full time.
unknowns: How current the aerial data are.
research_questions: Do layouts change less after the site visit?

incremental.description: PV installer reports roofs where the aerial data were wrong.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: changed or shaded roofs where aerial data are old, so most roofs are measured in full and shading judged on site (8.2); high: about 80% of addresses with current aerial data as assumed (21.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Draw the roof with existing building features, lay out the modules, mark equipment and cable routes, and check the final diagram of layouts and locations for PV arrays and equipment.

steps.what: PV installer draws the roof with existing building or site features: vents, skylights and edges
PV installer lays out the modules with setbacks and spacing
PV installer marks the inverter location and cable routes on the diagram
PV installer checks the final layout diagram

tasks.design: The layout starts from the roof model of the site survey with existing features already placed, instead of a hand sketch. The design tool places modules within setback and spacing rules, and the installer moves or removes them where the roof needs it. Inverter, cable routes and other equipment are drawn from a symbol library. The installer checks the final diagram.
tasks.previous_blocker: Layouts were sketched by hand from site measurements.
tasks.enabler_now: Design tools with roof models and placement rules.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing where a cable run will be hard to install.

reach.learn: Whether clearer diagrams cut rework on the roof.

evidence.claim: Employers must keep up-to-date diagrams of every electrical installation.
Design tools place modules within setback rules on a roof model.

assumptions: Boundary: drawing layouts and locations; protection device locations (task 17747) are decided in a sibling task.
Input contract for s1: the roof model from the site survey in task 17754, for about 80% of roofs; s1 is priced at that share.
research_questions: Do layout changes on installation day fall?

incremental.description: PV installer keeps setback rules and the symbol library current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: irregular roofs with many obstacles, so the roof model needs much redrawing and many modules are placed by hand (14.7); high: simple roofs with good roof models (34.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Count parts from the layout, determine materials and equipment, plan installation sequences, prepare and check the final order, and send it to the wholesaler.

steps.what: PV installer counts modules, rails, clamps and cables from the layout
PV installer determines materials and equipment for the job
PV installer plans installation sequences and tools to maximize installation efficiency
PV installer prepares the material order with article codes and prices
PV installer checks the final order: lines and quantities match the materials decided, and the delivery date and site are right
PV installer sends the approved order to the wholesaler

approvals.approved_version: The order lines, quantities and delivery date exactly as checked by the installer in s5, sent once electronically to the wholesaler for delivery to this job's site; any change needs a new check before sending.

tasks.design: The design tool turns the module layout into a parts list of modules, rails, clamps and cables by the mounting system's rules, instead of counting by hand. Chosen materials get article codes and prices from the sector's product data hub and become an electronic order, which the installer checks and sends. Deciding materials and planning the sequence stay with the installer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Parts were counted by hand and orders typed from catalogues.
tasks.enabler_now: Design tools with parts rules and product data hubs linked to ordering.
tasks.human_edge: Planning the day so the team is never waiting for material.
tasks.altitude: Less counting and typing; planning stays.

reach.learn: Whether electronic orders cut wrong deliveries.

evidence.claim: A product and price data hub for the installation sector connects to installer software.
An installation ERP handles material ordering and call-off.

assumptions: Boundary: materials, sequence and ordering for a job; system design (task 17749) and mechanical design choices (task 17760) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: the module layout from task 17750 and the mounting system's rules loaded in the design tool.
Input contract for s4: article codes and prices from the product data hub, covering about 90% of items.
Deciding, planning, checking and sending keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of jobs with non-standard parts.
research_questions: Do missing parts on installation day fall?

incremental.description: PV installer keeps preferred articles and mounting rules current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many non-standard parts outside the mounting rules and the data hub, so counting and typing stay for many lines (16.5); high: standard roofs with items in the hub (30.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather string and inverter data, calculate sizes and ratings, determine appropriate sizes, ratings and locations for overcurrent, disconnect, grounding and surge suppression devices, and draw them in the single-line diagram.

steps.what: PV installer gathers string voltages and currents, inverter specifications and cable lengths
PV installer calculates sizes and ratings from the standard's tables
PV installer determines appropriate sizes, ratings and locations for overcurrent, disconnect, grounding and surge suppression equipment
PV installer draws the devices in the single-line diagram

tasks.design: String voltages and currents come from the layout and module and inverter datasheets kept in the design tool, instead of being looked up per job. A calculation sheet built on the standard's tables computes fuse, breaker, cable and surge device ratings, and the installer checks them. Choosing devices and their locations stays with the installer. The single-line diagram is drawn from the chosen devices with standard symbols and kept up to date as the installation changes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Ratings were worked out from printed tables for each job.
tasks.enabler_now: Design tools with datasheet libraries and rule-based calculation sheets.
tasks.still_hard: Existing installations that do not match their old drawings.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that the existing meter cupboard cannot take another device.

evidence.claim: Building installations must meet the national electrical installation standard.
Up-to-date diagrams of every electrical installation are required.

assumptions: Boundary: sizing and placing protection devices; connection interfaces with the grid (task 17748) and circuit current requirements (task 17751) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: module and inverter datasheets kept in the design tool by the office; layouts from task 17750.
Input contract for s2: the calculation sheet maintained against the current edition of the standard.
unknowns: Share of jobs on existing installations with unknown wiring.
research_questions: Do inspection remarks on protection devices fall?

incremental.description: PV installer checks the calculation sheet after each new edition of the standard.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older installations where string and cable data need site investigation and the sheet covers few cases (20.5); high: standard new installations (37.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
